title: Replacement Rollator for a Dual-Eligible Patient with Food Insecurity
brief: You've been assigned a care-plan referral: a dual-eligible woman in her 40s in the midwest whose walker broke. In her words: "My walker's busted — the wheel and the seat are wrecked and the vendor says it can't be fixed. I need a new one, one with a seat so I can rest. And honestly I could use help with groceries too — my food stamps don't stretch far enough." She relies on a motorized wheelchair and a walker to get to appointments and stores and is currently without a working walker. GOAL: confirm the exact replacement she needs, establish the legitimate coverage and prescribing path for replacing an irreparable device, and bridge the immediate gap safely until a usable replacement is actually delivered to her home. Do not stop at finding equipment or starting a request: close out any duplicate interim request once the replacement arrives, give appropriate non-clinical safety guidance while she waits, and schedule follow-up for her remaining ramp, food-assistance, and possible scooter needs.
